endorsements.quote: The current curriculum could evolve to introduce AI concepts, tools, and applications specific to otolaryngology, ensuring that trainees are adept at leveraging AI for diagnostic imaging, patient monitoring, and surgical planning.
Furthermore, practical training on integrating AI-assisted diagnostic and therapeutic tools into everyday clinical practice will ensure that otolaryngologists remain at the forefront of patient care.

Workshops, seminars, and online courses focused on the latest AI tools, such as deep learning algorithms for classifying otitis media or AI systems for voice disorder assessments, should become a staple of professional development [ 3 ].

unlisted_practices: Introduce AI concepts and applications specific to otolaryngology into medical training curricula.
Use large language models to simulate patient interactions and clinical scenarios so trainees can practice diagnostic reasoning in a risk-free environment.
Integrate ethical considerations of patient consent, data privacy, and algorithmic bias into AI educational initiatives.
Create collaborative learning environments where clinicians, AI researchers, and bioethicists engage in dialogue on AI.
Conduct further research to institute and curate guidelines for professionals on AI use.

screen.reason: Editorial discussing the integration of AI into otolaryngology and recommending frameworks for AI education, training, and ethical governance.
